## Intent
Hypothesis: a branchless blend of alive/dead particle states with per-particle hash RNG can avoid branch-misprediction overhead and approach the streaming ceiling.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/particle AoS layout offers 32 hot bytes (47%) to loop 1 — age, pos, seed, vel — and 28 hot bytes (41%) to loop 2 — color, pos — leaving 53–59% of every cacheline as dead weight. No intermediate storage; the death verdict stays in registers, forcing respawn logic inline. The blend approach intended to select alive or respawned state without jumps. All measured working sets exceed L1d (spill at N≈481) and L2 (spill at N≈7710); N=10K–100K are L3-resident, N=1M–10M are DRAM.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p curve is flat across N within each death rate: q=0.01 ranges 25.1–27.0 ns/p, q=0.5 ranges 33.2–33.8 ns/p. The L3→DRAM transition at N≈247K causes only a ~1.5 ns/p uptick (25.2→27.0 at q=0.01), far smaller than a bandwidth-bound transition. This flatness signals per-particle overhead, not working-set residency, sets cost — no hidden cache knee.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth is 2.0–2.7 GB/s against the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — 16–21%. The memory floor is 5.359 ns/p; this algo runs at 25–34 ns/p, 4.7–6.3x the floor, confirming it is frontend-bound (67–73% frontend stall), not bandwidth-bound. The algo ties naive scalar (0.95–1.01x baseline everywhere) and loses to the winner by 1.75–3.27x: widest at q=0.01 (3.27x at N=100K) where the winner's cross-particle vectorization is unobscured, narrowest at q=0.5 (1.75x at N=1M) where respawn compute dominates both. Cost scales 25→33 ns/p from q=0.01→0.5 but branch_flush stays 0% — respawn arithmetic, not misprediction.

## Assembly
The codegen did not realize the branchless blend. The 383-instruction body is heavily branchy: 25 cmp, 12 vucomiss, 12 cmovae, 10 jae, 6 je, 6 jne, 6 jmp. Death decision uses vucomiss+jbe; respawn chains je/jne/jmp. Vectorization is intra-particle only: vmulps/vaddps on 3–4 components of one particle (`vmulps xmm8,xmm8,xmm4` for pos+=vel*dt) with vbroadcastss to splat dt — no cross-particle SIMD. Loop 2 uses byte-granular scatter (`mov BYTE PTR [rsi+rdi*1],r10b`). The complex control flow explains the 67–73% frontend stall: decode cannot feed the backend.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.95–1.01x of naive baseline at every N×q point and 1.75–3.27x slower than the winner. The branchless blend was never realized: vucomiss+jbe and je/jne branches dominate the 383-instruction body, producing 67–73% frontend stall that caps bandwidth at 16–21% of ceiling. Intra-particle-only vmulps cannot amortize the 53% dead bytes in the 68 B/p layout, and the scalar per-particle loop cannot match the winner's cross-particle auto-vectorization.
